items.path: AMD CBS > CPU Common Options > CPU Speculative Store Modes
items.menu: AMD CBS > CPU Common Options
items.name: CPU Speculative Store Modes
items.help:
Balanced:
Store instructions may delay sending out their invalidations to remote cacheline copies when the cacheline is present but not in a writable state in the local cache.

More Speculative:
Store instructions will send out invalidations to remote cacheline copies as soon as possible.

Less Speculative:
Store instructions may delay sending out their invalidations to remote cacheline copies when the cacheline is not present in the local cache or not in a writable state in the local cache.

items.menu: AMD CBS > UMC Common Options > DDR Options > DDR Timing Configuration > Accept
items.name: Memory Target Speed
items.help:
Specifies the memory target speed in MT/s. The valid input is 2000 MT/s, 2400MT/s, and range of 3200MT/s ~ 11200 MT/s(stepping of 200 MT/s). The Value is in decimal.
The user input value will be rounded down to align with the stepping of 200MT/s.
The Maximum speed defined in the JEDEC spec is 8400MT/s, any input value that is greater than 8400MT/s will be limited to 8400MT/s.

items.path: AMD CBS > NBIO Common Options > PSPP Policy
items.menu: AMD CBS > NBIO Common Options
items.name: PSPP Policy
items.help:
PSPP - PCIe Speed Power Policy
PSPP - Balanced
AC Policy = PCIe Gen 5 devices are allowed to run at PCIe Gen 5.  No throttling will be applied.
DC Policy = PCIe Gen 5 devices will be transitioned to PCIe Gen 3 upon AC to DC transition.  The speed will be restored upon transition back to AC power. 
PSPP - Performance
AC Policy = PCIe Gen 5 devices are allowed to run at PCIe Gen 5.  No throttling will be applied.
DC Policy = PCIe Gen 5 devices will be transitioned to PCIe Gen 4 upon AC to DC transition.  The speed will be restored upon transition back to AC power. 
(Default) = Balanced and is AMD's recommended configuration.

items.path: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control > Microsoft Security Levels
items.menu: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control
items.name: Microsoft Security Levels
items.help:
This option provide one stop configuration for SCPC (Note: Firmware Anti-rollback is excluded). 
For Level 1, it will configure TPM, SVM, IOMMU, SecureBoot; 
For Level 2, it will configure TPM, SVM, IOMMU, DMAr, SecureBIO, SecureBoot; 
For Level 3, it will configure TPM, SMM Isolation, SVM, IOMMU, DMAr, TSME, SecureBIO, SecureBoot, Modern Standby. 
Regard TPM configuration, dTPM refers to discrete TPM. Pluton fTPM refers to Pluton firmware TPM. ASP fTPM refers to ASP firmware TPM. 
NOTE: FAR is required for Level3 and please enable it manually in CBS-> SOC Miscellaneous Control / Firmware Anti-rollback (FAR) / FAR Switch.

dTPM with Pluton security processor is recommend configuration for Level1/2/3

options.text: dTPM Level 1 without Pluton Security Processor
dTPM Level 2 without Pluton Security Processor
dTPM Level 3 without Pluton Security Processor
dTPM Level 1 with Pluton Security Processor
dTPM Level 2 with Pluton Security Processor
dTPM Level 3 with Pluton Security Processor

items.name: Secured-core Auto enablement
items.help:
If set to Disable, AGESA will delete EFI variable 'BuiltAsSecuredCorePC' if detected
If set to Enable, AGESA will set EFI variable 'BuiltAsSecuredCorePC' to non-zero value
If 'BuiltAsSecuredCorePC' set to non-zero, it will identify a device as Secure-core PC
More detials refer to 'Secured-Core PC Identifier' in MSFT document.
If set to Auto, ignore, AGESA will do nothing

items.path: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control > Firmware Anti-rollback (FAR) > Initial SPL value for FAR
items.menu: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control > Firmware Anti-rollback (FAR)
items.name: Initial SPL value for FAR
items.help:
Initial SPL value is only applicable when FAR switch is enabled.

0 = initial SPL value is not set, SPL fuse will always follow the SPL value in the SPL table.

Not 0 = if FAR has been enforced, BIOS will keep SPL fuse as it is. otherwise,  BIOS will enforce FAR and set SPL fuse to this initial SPL value.

items.path: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control > Firmware Anti-rollback (FAR) > FAR Switch
items.menu: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control > Firmware Anti-rollback (FAR)
items.name: FAR Switch
items.help:
Enabled  = if initial SPL value is 0, and FAR is NOT enforced, BIOS will enforce FAR and set SPL fuse to SPL value in the SPL table.
        if initial SPL value is 0, and FAR is enforced, BIOS will update SPL fuse to SPL value in the SPL table.
     if initial SPL value is not 0, and FAR is NOT enforced, BIOS will enforce FAR and set SPL fuse to initial SPL value.
     if initial SPL value is not 0, and FAR is enforced, BIOS will keep SPL fuse as it is.

Disabled = BIOS will NOT change FAR enforcement state and NOT set SPL fuse.

SDW0(4MDATA) +  SDW1(1MDATA) ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0x3 
Mainstream Desktop (AM5 Package)  
HDA(3SDI) +  PDM(2CH)(Default) ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0x4
HDA(1SDI) +  PDM(6CH) ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0x5 
HDA(1SDI) + SDW0(1MDATA) + PDM(2CH) ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0x6 
SDW0(4MDATA) + PDM(6CH) ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0x7 
SDW0(4MDATA) + SDW1(1MDATA) + PDM(2CH) ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0x8 
Mainstream notebook  
3I2S PORTS + 1 REFCLK + 1 INTR ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0x9
HDA(3SDI) +  PDM(6CH) +I2S(Default) ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0xA 
HDA(3SDI) +  PDM(8CH)  ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0xB 
HDA(1SDI) + SDW0(1MDATA) + PDM(6CH) + I2S ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0xC 
SDW0(4MDATA)+ SDW1(1MDATA) + PDM(6CH) + I2S  ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0xD 
SDW0(4MDATA) + SDW1(1MDATA)+ PDM(8CH)  ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0xE 
LPFLL Clock out for lab debug  
LPFLL Clock out  ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0xF

items.path: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control > Microsoft Security Levels
items.menu: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control
items.name: Microsoft Security Levels
items.help:
This option provide one stop configuration for SCPC (Note: Firmware Anti-rollback is excluded). 
For Level 1, it will configure TPM, SVM, IOMMU, SecureBoot; 
For Level 2, it will configure TPM, SVM, IOMMU, DMAr, SecureBIO, SecureBoot; 
For Level 3, it will configure TPM, SMM Isolation, SVM, IOMMU, DMAr, TSME, SecureBIO, SecureBoot, Modern Standby. 
Regard TPM configuration, dTPM refers to discrete TPM. Pluton fTPM refers to Pluton firmware TPM. ASP fTPM refers to ASP firmware TPM. 
NOTE: FAR is required for Level3 and please enable it manually in CBS-> SOC Miscellaneous Control / Firmware Anti-rollback (FAR) / FAR Switch.

dTPM with Pluton security processor is recommend configuration for Level1/2/3

options.text: dTPM Level 1 without Pluton Security Processor
dTPM Level 2 without Pluton Security Processor
dTPM Level 3 without Pluton Security Processor
dTPM Level 1 with Pluton Security Processor
dTPM Level 2 with Pluton Security Processor
dTPM Level 3 with Pluton Security Processor

items.path: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control > Firmware Anti-rollback (FAR) > Initial SPL value for FAR

items.name: Initial SPL value for FAR
items.help:
Initial SPL value is only applicable when FAR switch is enabled.

0 = initial SPL value is not set, SPL fuse will always follow the SPL value in the SPL table.

Not 0 = if FAR has been enforced, BIOS will keep SPL fuse as it is. otherwise,  BIOS will enforce FAR and set SPL fuse to this initial SPL value.

items.path: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control > Firmware Anti-rollback (FAR) > FAR Switch
items.menu: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control > Firmware Anti-rollback (FAR)
items.name: FAR Switch
items.help:
Enabled  = if initial SPL value is 0, and FAR is NOT enforced, BIOS will enforce FAR and set SPL fuse to SPL value in the SPL table.
        if initial SPL value is 0, and FAR is enforced, BIOS will update SPL fuse to SPL value in the SPL table.
     if initial SPL value is not 0, and FAR is NOT enforced, BIOS will enforce FAR and set SPL fuse to initial SPL value.
     if initial SPL value is not 0, and FAR is enforced, BIOS will keep SPL fuse as it is.

Disabled = BIOS will NOT change FAR enforcement state and NOT set SPL fuse.

Specifies the memory target speed in MT/s. The valid input is 2000 MT/s, 2400MT/s, and range of 3200MT/s ~ 12000 MT/s(stepping of 200 MT/s). The Value is in decimal.

SDW0(4MDATA) + PDM(6CH)              ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0x7 
SDW0(4MDATA) + SDW1(1MDATA) + PDM(2CH) 
 ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0x8 
SW0(3MDATA) + SW1(2MDATA) + PDM(2CH)  
 ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0x11
Mainstream notebook  
3I2S PORTS + 1 REFCLK + 1 INTR     ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0x9
HDA(3SDI) +  PDM(6CH) +I2S(Default)  ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0xA

SW0(3MDATA) + SW1(2MDATA) + PDM(8CH)  
ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0x12
SW0(3MDATA) + SW1(2MDATA) + PDM(6CH) + I2S 
 ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0x13
2I2S + 1 INTR + PDM(4CH)             ACP_PIN_CONFIG[3:0]  = 0x14
LPFLL Clock out for lab debug

items.path: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control > Microsoft Security Levels
items.menu: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control
items.name: Microsoft Security Levels
items.help:
This option provide one stop configuration for SCPC (Note: Firmware Anti-rollback is excluded). 
For Level 1, it will configure TPM, SVM, IOMMU, SecureBoot; 
For Level 2, it will configure TPM, SVM, IOMMU, DMAr, SecureBIO, SecureBoot; 
For Level 3, it will configure TPM, SMM Isolation, SVM, IOMMU, DMAr, TSME, SecureBIO, SecureBoot, Modern Standby. 
Regard TPM configuration, dTPM refers to discrete TPM. Pluton fTPM refers to Pluton firmware TPM. ASP fTPM refers to ASP firmware TPM. 
NOTE: FAR is required for Level3 and please enable it manually in CBS-> SOC Miscellaneous Control / Firmware Anti-rollback (FAR) / FAR Switch.

dTPM with Pluton security processor is recommend configuration for Level1/2/3

options.text: dTPM Level 1 without Pluton Security Processor
dTPM Level 2 without Pluton Security Processor
dTPM Level 3 without Pluton Security Processor
dTPM Level 1 with Pluton Security Processor
dTPM Level 2 with Pluton Security Processor
dTPM Level 3 with Pluton Security Processor
Pluton fTPM Level 1 with Pluton Security Processor
Pluton fTPM Level 2 with Pluton Security Processor
Pluton fTPM Level 3 with Pluton Security Processor
ASP fTPM Level 1 without Pluton Security Processor
ASP fTPM Level 2 without Pluton Security Processor
ASP fTPM Level 1 with Pluton Security Processor
ASP fTPM Level 2 with Pluton Security Processor

items.menu: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control
items.name: Secured-core Auto enablement
items.help:
If set to Disable, AGESA will delete EFI variable 'BuiltAsSecuredCorePC' if detected
If set to Enable, AGESA will set EFI variable 'BuiltAsSecuredCorePC' to non-zero value
If 'BuiltAsSecuredCorePC' set to non-zero, it will identify a device as Secure-core PC
More detials refer to 'Secured-Core PC Identifier' in MSFT document.
If set to Auto, ignore, AGESA will do nothing

items.path: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control > Firmware Anti-rollback (FAR) > Initial SPL value for FAR
items.menu: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control > Firmware Anti-rollback (FAR)
items.name: Initial SPL value for FAR
items.help:
Initial SPL value is only applicable when FAR switch is enabled.

0 = initial SPL value is not set, SPL fuse will always follow the SPL value in the SPL table.

Not 0 = if FAR has been enforced, BIOS will keep SPL fuse as it is. otherwise,  BIOS will enforce FAR and set SPL fuse to this initial SPL value.

items.path: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control > Firmware Anti-rollback (FAR) > FAR Switch
items.menu: AMD CBS > SOC Miscellaneous Control > Firmware Anti-rollback (FAR)
items.name: FAR Switch
items.help:
Enabled  = if initial SPL value is 0, and FAR is NOT enforced, BIOS will enforce FAR and set SPL fuse to SPL value in the SPL table.
        if initial SPL value is 0, and FAR is enforced, BIOS will update SPL fuse to SPL value in the SPL table.
     if initial SPL value is not 0, and FAR is NOT enforced, BIOS will enforce FAR and set SPL fuse to initial SPL value.
     if initial SPL value is not 0, and FAR is enforced, BIOS will keep SPL fuse as it is.

Disabled = BIOS will NOT change FAR enforcement state and NOT set SPL fuse.

items.path: Configuration Options > Array Management > Create Array > Select RAID Level:
items.menu: Configuration Options > Array Management > Create Array
items.name: Select RAID Level:
items.help:
Selects the desired RAID level. The configuration utility supports Volume, RAIDAble, RAID 0, RAID 1, and RAID 5 and RAID 10.

VOLUME --  Single disk or concatenation of disks (JBOD).
RAIDABLE -- RAID aware single disk for future redundancy.
RAID 0 -- Uses disk striping to provide high data throughput.
RAID 1 -- Uses disk mirroring to provide an exact copy for data redundancy.
RAID 5 -- uses striping with parity to balance between performance and data integrity. Parity data allows the Array to be recreated in the event of a single disk failure.
RAID 10 -- uses mirrored data striping to offer both performance and data redundancy.

items.path: Configuration Options > Array Management > Create Array > Array Size:
items.menu: Configuration Options > Array Management > Create Array
items.name: Array Size:
items.help: Allows the user to specify the size of the Array to be created. A value of 0 will be reset to the maximum supported Array size when a valid configuration has been selected.

items.path: Configuration Options > Array Management > Create Array > Array Size Unit:
items.menu: Configuration Options > Array Management > Create Array
items.name: Array Size Unit:
items.help: Selects the units in which the Array Size is displayed. 1 MB = 1000 KBs. 1GB = 1000 MBs. 1 TB = 1000 GBs.

items.path: Configuration Options > Array Management > Create Array > Select CacheTagSize:
items.menu: Configuration Options > Array Management > Create Array
items.name: Select CacheTagSize:
items.help: Specifies the Cachetag Size. This is the amount of data per disk in a stripe. Supported sizes are 64KB, 128KB, or 256KB.

items.path: Configuration Options > Array Management > Create Array > Select CacheTagSize:
items.menu: Configuration Options > Array Management > Create Array
items.name: Select CacheTagSize:
items.help: Specifies the Cachetag Size. This is the amount of data per disk in a stripe. Supported sizes are 64KB, 128KB, or 256KB.

items.path: Configuration Options > Array Management > Create Array > Read Cache Policy:
items.menu: Configuration Options > Array Management > Create Array
items.name: Read Cache Policy:
items.help:
Selects the desired read policy.  The configuration utility supports No Cache and Read Cache.

Read Cache -- Read data will be pre-fetched
No Cache -- Reads will be performed only when requested

items.path: Configuration Options > Array Management > Create Array > Write Cache Policy:
items.menu: Configuration Options > Array Management > Create Array
items.name: Write Cache Policy:
items.help:
Selects the desired write policy.  The configuration utility supports No Cache and Write Back Cache.

No Cache -- Writes are done immediately
Write Back Cache -- Writes are delayed.  May result in loss of data in event of system failure!

items.path: Configuration Options > Array Management > Create Array > Select Physical Disks > Select Media Type:
items.menu: Configuration Options > Array Management > Create Array > Select Physical Disks
items.name: Select Media Type:
items.help:
Selects the physical disk media type.

HDD - Rotational magnetic media.
SSD - Solid State Disk.

items.name: USB Device Power on (USB32_1)

Because AM5 socket CPU and AGESA might be updated, the function of this option will be subject to change without notice.

This feature might affect ability of Hibernate.

items.name: CPU Frequency
items.help: Specifies a custom CPU core frequency. Should be combined with a custom CPU voltage. Power saving features for idle cores (e.g. cc6 sleep) remain active. Manual CPU OC overrides PBO settings.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking > CPU Voltage
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking
items.name: CPU Voltage
items.help: Specifies a custom CPU core voltage (mV). Should be combined with a custom CPU core frequency. Power saving features for idle cores (e.g. cc6 sleep) remain active. stepping is 5mv. Voltage ranges allowed to be set will be limited outside of LN2 mode. If in LN2 mode (and CPU temp is below -40c) the allowable range of settable voltages will be extended.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking > CPU Core Count Control > SMT Control
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking > CPU Core Count Control
items.name: SMT Control
items.help: Can be used to disable symmetric multithreading. To re-enable SMT, a POWER CYCLE is needed after selecting the 'Auto' option.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking > CPU Core Count Control > Down Core Mode
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking > CPU Core Count Control
items.name: Down Core Mode

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual iGPU Overclocking > GFX Clock Frequency
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual iGPU Overclocking
items.name: GFX Clock Frequency
items.help: Specifies a custom GFX core frequency. Must be combined with a custom GFX voltage. Power saving features (like GFX Pstates) remain active

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual iGPU Overclocking > GFX Voltage
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual iGPU Overclocking
items.name: GFX Voltage
items.help: Specifies a custom GFX core voltage (mV). Must be combined with a custom GFX frequency. GFX voltage is derived from SOC / uncore voltage rail. Power saving features (like GFX Pstates) remain active.

items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options
items.name: DDR5 Nitro Mode
items.help: Can improve overclocked memory support for modules over 6000Mt/s with potential boot time and/or latency tradeoffs

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options > DDR5 Robust Training Mode
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options
items.name: DDR5 Robust Training Mode
items.help: A more comprehensive memory training algorithm that increases boot time but can result in improved stability at overclocked memory settings

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options > Nitro RX Data
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options
items.name: Nitro RX Data
items.help: Configures the RX timing between memory controller and PHY.  Higher value may enable increased memory frequency at the expense of increased latency.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options > Nitro TX Data

items.name: Nitro TX Data
items.help: Configures the TX timing between memory controller and PHY. Higher value may enable increased memory frequency at the expense of increased latency.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options > Nitro Control Line
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options
items.name: Nitro Control Line
items.help: Configures the command timing latency between the memory controller and PHY. Higher value may enable increased memory frequency at the expense of increased latency.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options > Nitro Rx Burst Length
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options
items.name: Nitro Rx Burst Length
items.help:
DQ Training Pattern Length -
  Higher number results in more robust training and longer runtime.
  Lower number results in less robust training and shorter runtime, but potentially less stability.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options > PHY RX Data P0 Ctrl
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options
items.name: PHY RX Data P0 Ctrl
items.help: Auto: Follow default setting, Manual: Manually specify

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options > PHY RX Data P0
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options
items.name: PHY RX Data P0
items.help:
Valid values: 0x0 - 0xF. Configures the RX timing between memory controller and PHY. Each bit in the 4 binary digits represents a pipe stage in the umc to ddrphy path, less means less latency, more means more stability at high frequency
0001 or 0100 - enable 1 pipe stage
0111 or 1110 - enable 3 pipe stages
1111 - enable all 4 pipe stages

rules.suppress_if: [DDR5 Nitro Mode]=0x1 NOT [PHY RX Data P0 Ctrl]=0x1 NOT OR

items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options > DDR Timing Configuration
items.name: Memory Target Speed
items.help:
Specifies the memory target speed in MT/s. The valid input is 2000 MT/s, 2400MT/s, and range of 3200MT/s ~ 12000 MT/s(stepping of 200 MT/s). The Value is in decimal.
The user input value will be rounded down to align with the stepping of 200MT/s.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > Precision Boost Overdrive
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive
items.name: Precision Boost Overdrive
items.help:
Precision Boost Overdrive:
  Enabled: Allows Processor to run beyond defined values for PPT, VDD_CPU EDC, VDD_CPU TDC, VDD_SOC EDC, VDD_SOC TDC to the limits of the board, and allows it to boost at higher voltages for longer durations than default operation.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > PBO Limits
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive
items.name: PBO Limits
items.help: Default: Loads AMD default socket power (PPT), electrically-limited VRM current (EDC), and thermally-limited VRM current (TDC) limits. Motherboard: Allows the processor to run according to increased PPT, EDC, and TDC limits defined by your motherboard. Manual: Allows the processor to ignore AMD default limits for PPT, EDC, and TDC and instead use manual values (up to the maximum capabilities of the of the motherboard).

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > PPT Limit [mW]
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive
items.name: PPT Limit [mW]
items.help: Adjust total CPU socket power delivery capability. Adjustable up to the limit supported by your motherboard.

rules.suppress_if: [Precision Boost Overdrive]=0x2 NOT [PBO Limits]=0x2 NOT OR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > TDC Limit [mA]
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive
items.name: TDC Limit [mA]
items.help: Adjust peak current from your motherboard's CPU core VRM phases in thermally-limited scenarios. Adjustable up to the limit supported by your motherboard.

rules.suppress_if: [Precision Boost Overdrive]=0x2 NOT [PBO Limits]=0x2 NOT OR

items.name: EDC Limit [mA]
items.help: Adjust peak current from your motherboard CPU core VRM phases in electrically-limited scenarios. Adjustable up to the limit supported by your motherboard.

rules.suppress_if: [Precision Boost Overdrive]=0x2 NOT [PBO Limits]=0x2 NOT OR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > GFX Curve Optimizer > GFX Curve Optimizer
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > GFX Curve Optimizer
items.name: GFX Curve Optimizer
items.help: Allows the user to shift the GFX Voltage / Frequency (AVFS) curve to include higher voltages (positive values) or lower voltages (negative values). The larger the value entered the larger the magnitude of the voltage shift.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > GFX Curve Optimizer > GFX Curve Optimizer Sign
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > GFX Curve Optimizer
items.name: GFX Curve Optimizer Sign
items.help: Determines the direction of the curve shift for GFX. Positive shifts the curve up to use higher voltages. Negative shifts the curve down to use lower voltages

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > GFX Curve Optimizer > GFX Curve Optimizer Magnitude
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > GFX Curve Optimizer
items.name: GFX Curve Optimizer Magnitude
items.help: Determines the magnitude of the GFX curve shift to be made (entered in whole numbers) the larger the value entered the larger the magnitude of the shift.Field Defaults to 0 and is user enterable in whole integer numbers. Value entered, combined with the sign above, is the used to send the SMU an GFX Curve Optimizer

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > Curve Optimizer > Curve Optimizer
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > Curve Optimizer
items.name: Curve Optimizer
items.help: Allows the user to shift the Voltage / Frequency (AVFS) curve to include higher voltages (positive values) or lower voltages (negative values). The larger the value entered the larger the magnitude of the voltage shift

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > Curve Optimizer > All Core Curve Optimizer Sign
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > Curve Optimizer
items.name: All Core Curve Optimizer Sign
items.help: Determines the direction of the curve shift on all cores. Positive shifts the curve up to use higher voltages. Negative shifts the curve down to use lower voltages

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > VDDP Voltage Control > VDDP Voltage Control
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > VDDP Voltage Control
items.name: VDDP Voltage Control
items.help: Allows the user to adjust the VDDP voltage.'Manual' means set voltage for the DDR bus signaling (PHY),. 'Auto' means VDDP is system default.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > VDDP Voltage Control > VDDP Voltage Adjust
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > VDDP Voltage Control
items.name: VDDP Voltage Adjust
items.help: VDDP is a voltage for the DDR bus signaling (PHY), and it is derived from your DRAM Voltage (VDDIO_Mem). As a result, VDDP voltage in mV can approach but not exceed your DRAM Voltage

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > SoC/Uncore OC Mode > SoC/Uncore OC Mode
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > SoC/Uncore OC Mode
items.name: SoC/Uncore OC Mode
items.help: Forces CPU SoC/uncore components (e.g. Infinity Fabric, memory, and integrated graphics) to run at their maximum specified frequency at all times. May improve performance at the expense of idle power savings

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > SoC Voltage > SoC Voltage
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > SoC Voltage
items.name: SoC Voltage
items.help: Specifies the SoC/uncore voltage (VDD_SOC) in mV to support memory and Infinity Fabric overclocking. VDD_SOC also determines the GPU voltage on processors with integrated graphics. Voltage ranges allowed to be set will be limited outside of LN2 mode. If in LN2 mode (and CPU temp is below -40c) the allowable range of settable voltages will be extended.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > LN2 Mode > LN2 Mode
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > LN2 Mode
items.name: LN2 Mode
items.help: Enables settings that provide additional stability at extreme cold operating temperatures

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > VDD Misc > VDD Misc Control
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > VDD Misc
items.name: VDD Misc Control
items.help: Allows the user to adjust the VDD Misc voltage.'Manual' means set voltage for the GMI PHY,. 'Auto' means VDD MISC is system default.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > VDD Misc > VDD Misc Voltage
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > VDD Misc
items.name: VDD Misc Voltage
items.help: specific the VDD Misc Voltage in mV, definitely follow SVI3 type 2 Slave VID(500~5600mV step 10mV). Voltage ranges allowed to be set will be limited outside of LN2 mode. If in LN2 mode (and CPU temp is below -40c) the allowable range of settable voltages will be extended.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > LCLK Frequency Control > LCLK Frequency Control
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > LCLK Frequency Control
items.name: LCLK Frequency Control
items.help: AUTO: Default Settings. Manual: manually configure LCLK Frequency. Only specific frequencies are permitted; processor firmware will automatically round UP to the nearest permitted frequency.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > LCLK Frequency Control > Minimun Frequency
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > LCLK Frequency Control
items.name: Minimun Frequency
items.help: Minimum LCLK Frequency. Set minimum and maximun to the same value for fixed frequency operation.Range:150MHz ~ 2500MHz

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > LCLK Frequency Control > Maximum Frequency
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > LCLK Frequency Control
items.name: Maximum Frequency
items.help: Maximum LCLK Frequency. Set minimum and maximun to the same value for fixed frequency operation.Range:150MHz ~ 2500MHz

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control > VDDIO Ctrl
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control
items.name: VDDIO Ctrl
items.help: Allows the user to adjust the VDDIO voltage.'Manual' means set DIMM VDD/VDDQ will synchronize to APU VDDIO. 'Separate' means independent control of APU VDDIO,DIMM VDD/VDDQ.Note, that running VDDQ != VDD is non-standard and may casue memory stability issues. Take care that during ramp down and ramp up,the VDDq-VDD voltage must less than 200mv.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control > PMIC VDD Stepping Control
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control
items.name: PMIC VDD Stepping Control
items.help: PMIC VDD Stepping Control by R2B, select 10mv will set PMIC R2B BIT5

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control > DIMM VDD Adjust
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control
items.name: DIMM VDD Adjust
items.help: Adjust DIMM Power Supply, stepping is 10mV. Range is from 800mV to 1430mV.Take care that during ramp down and ramp up,the VDDq-VDD voltage must less than 200mv.

rules.suppress_if: [Q0xf0]=0x2 [PMIC VDD Stepping Control]=0x1 OR [VDDIO Ctrl]=0x1 NOT [VDDIO Ctrl]=0x2 NOT AND OR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control > DIMM VDD Adjust
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control
items.name: DIMM VDD Adjust
items.help: Adjust DIMM Power Supply, stepping is 10mV. Range is from 800mV to 1650mV.Take care that during ramp down and ramp up,the VDDq-VDD voltage must less than 200mv.

rules.suppress_if: [Q0xf0]=0x2 NOT [PMIC VDD Stepping Control]=0x1 NOT AND [VDDIO Ctrl]=0x1 NOT [VDDIO Ctrl]=0x2 NOT AND OR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control > PMIC VDDQ Stepping Control
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control
items.name: PMIC VDDQ Stepping Control
items.help: PMIC VDD Stepping Control by R2B, select 10mv will set PMIC R2B BIT4

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control > DIMM VDDQ Adjust
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control
items.name: DIMM VDDQ Adjust
items.help: Adjust DIMM DQ Power Supply, stepping is 10mV. Range is from 800mV to 1430mV.Take care that during ramp down and ramp up, the VDDq-VDD voltage must less than 200mv.And Vpp must always equal or greater than VDDQ

rules.suppress_if: [Q0xf0]=0x2 [PMIC VDDQ Stepping Control]=0x1 OR [VDDIO Ctrl]=0x2 NOT OR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control > DIMM VDDQ Adjust
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control
items.name: DIMM VDDQ Adjust
items.help: Adjust DIMM DQ Power Supply, stepping is 10mV. Range is from 800mV to 1650mV.Take care that during ramp down and ramp up, the VDDq-VDD voltage must less than 200mv.And Vpp must always equal or greater than VDDQ

rules.suppress_if: [Q0xf0]=0x2 NOT [PMIC VDDQ Stepping Control]=0x1 NOT AND [VDDIO Ctrl]=0x2 NOT OR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control > Enable Platform PMIC Control
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control
items.name: Enable Platform PMIC Control
items.help: When Enable Platform PMIC Control is enabled, the DDR PMIC voltages are not adjusted by processor FW, and may be adjusted directly by EC or other platform based mechanism.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VPP Voltage Control > VPP Ctrl
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VPP Voltage Control
items.name: VPP Ctrl
items.help: Auto: Follow default setting, Manual: Manually specify

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VPP Voltage Control > VPP Adjust
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VPP Voltage Control
items.name: VPP Adjust
items.help: Adjust MEM VPP, stepping is 10mV. Range is from 1500mV to 2135mV

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDD_MEM Voltage Control > VDD_MEM Control
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDD_MEM Voltage Control
items.name: VDD_MEM Control
items.help: Auto: Follow default setting, Manual: Manually specify the VDD_MEM Voltage since VDDP_DDR is source from it.VDD_MEM must greater 100mv than VDDP_DDR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking > CPU Frequency
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking
items.name: CPU Frequency
items.help: Specifies a custom CPU core frequency. Should be combined with a custom CPU VOLTAGE that is REQUIRED to be set by the user. Power saving features for idle cores (e.g. cc6 sleep) remain active. Manual CPU OC overrides PBO settings. Please note that the frequency cannot drop below 1200MHz on AMD Ryzen 9000 series processors.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking > CPU Voltage
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking
items.name: CPU Voltage
items.help: Specifies a custom CPU core voltage (mV). Should be combined with a custom CPU core frequency. Power saving features for idle cores (e.g. cc6 sleep) remain active. Stepping is 5mv. Voltage ranges allowed to be set will be limited outside of LN2 mode. If in LN2 mode (and CPU temp is below -40c) the allowable range of settable voltages will be extended.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking > Prochot VRM Throttling
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking
items.name: Prochot VRM Throttling
items.help: Disabling Prochot will disable the VRMs ability to throttle the CPU when the voltage regulator is approaching its thermal limits

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking > Peak Current Control
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking
items.name: Peak Current Control

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking > CPU Core Count Control > SMT Control
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking > CPU Core Count Control
items.name: SMT Control
items.help: Can be used to disable symmetric multithreading. To re-enable SMT, a POWER CYCLE is needed after selecting the 'Auto' option.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options > DDR5 Nitro Mode
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options
items.name: DDR5 Nitro Mode
items.help: Can improve overclocked memory support for modules over 6000Mt/s with potential boot time and/or latency tradeoffs

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options > DDR5 Robust Training Mode
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options
items.name: DDR5 Robust Training Mode
items.help: A more comprehensive memory training algorithm that increases boot time but can result in improved stability at overclocked memory settings

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options > Nitro RX Data
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options
items.name: Nitro RX Data
items.help: Configures the RX timing between memory controller and PHY.  Higher value may enable increased memory frequency at the expense of increased latency.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options > Nitro TX Data
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options
items.name: Nitro TX Data
items.help: Configures the TX timing between memory controller and PHY. Higher value may enable increased memory frequency at the expense of increased latency.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options > Nitro Control Line
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options
items.name: Nitro Control Line
items.help: Configures the command timing latency between the memory controller and PHY. Higher value may enable increased memory frequency at the expense of increased latency.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options > Nitro Rx Burst Length
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options
items.name: Nitro Rx Burst Length
items.help:
DQ Training Pattern Length -
  Higher number results in more robust training and longer runtime.
  Lower number results in less robust training and shorter runtime, but potentially less stability.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > Precision Boost Overdrive
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive
items.name: Precision Boost Overdrive
items.help:
Precision Boost Overdrive:
  Enabled: Allows Processor to run beyond defined values for PPT, VDD_CPU EDC, VDD_CPU TDC, VDD_SOC EDC, VDD_SOC TDC to the limits of the board, and allows it to boost at higher voltages for longer durations than default operation.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > PBO Limits
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive
items.name: PBO Limits
items.help: Default: Loads AMD default socket power (PPT), electrically-limited VRM current (EDC), and thermally-limited VRM current (TDC) limits. Motherboard: Allows the processor to run according to increased PPT, EDC, and TDC limits defined by your motherboard. Manual: Allows the processor to ignore AMD default limits for PPT, EDC, and TDC and instead use manual values (up to the maximum capabilities of the of the motherboard).

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > PPT Limit [mW]
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive
items.name: PPT Limit [mW]
items.help: Adjust total CPU socket power delivery capability. Adjustable up to the limit supported by your motherboard.

rules.suppress_if: [Precision Boost Overdrive]=0x2 NOT [PBO Limits]=0x2 NOT OR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > TDC Limit [mA]
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive
items.name: TDC Limit [mA]
items.help: Adjust peak current from your motherboard's CPU core VRM phases in thermally-limited scenarios. Adjustable up to the limit supported by your motherboard.

rules.suppress_if: [Precision Boost Overdrive]=0x2 NOT [PBO Limits]=0x2 NOT OR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > GFX Curve Optimizer > GFX Curve Optimizer
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > GFX Curve Optimizer
items.name: GFX Curve Optimizer
items.help: Allows the user to shift the GFX Voltage / Frequency (AVFS) curve to include higher voltages (positive values) or lower voltages (negative values). The larger the value entered the larger the magnitude of the voltage shift.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > GFX Curve Optimizer > GFX Curve Optimizer Sign
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > GFX Curve Optimizer
items.name: GFX Curve Optimizer Sign
items.help: Determines the direction of the curve shift for GFX. Positive shifts the curve up to use higher voltages. Negative shifts the curve down to use lower voltages

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > GFX Curve Optimizer > GFX Curve Optimizer Magnitude
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > GFX Curve Optimizer
items.name: GFX Curve Optimizer Magnitude
items.help: Determines the magnitude of the GFX curve shift to be made (entered in whole numbers) the larger the value entered the larger the magnitude of the shift.Field Defaults to 0 and is user enterable in whole integer numbers. Value entered, combined with the sign above, is the used to send the SMU an GFX Curve Optimizer

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > Curve Shaper > Min Frequency - Low Temperature
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > Curve Shaper
items.name: Min Frequency - Low Temperature
items.help:
Curve Shaper is an advanced overclocking tuning suite utilizing the same "Curve optimizer" steps. It changes variable voltage across all cores for finite (overlapping) frequency and temperature regions. This can be used to more precisely tune the voltage required by your system. 
In general, Low temperature corresponds to idle temps, Med Temperature corresponds to 1T/Gaming Workloads, and high temperature is for stress tests.
Additionally, Min and Low frequencies are idle/background tasks, Medium is high core count workloads, and high and Max frequency are for gaming and 1T workloads
These settings work as "bands" so you may find that for particular cases several settings impact the behavior. Ex, A workload running at 65 Celsius will likely be influenced by Low temp and Med temp values. Workloads lower than 65C will be more impacted by Low. Workloads above 65C will be more impacted by Medium.

items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > Curve Shaper
items.name: Min Frequency - Low Temperature Sign
items.help: Determines the direction of the shift. Positive shifts the curve up to use higher voltages. Negative shifts the curve down to use lower voltages

items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > Curve Shaper

items.help: Determines the magnitude of the shift to be made (entered in whole numbers) the larger the value entered the larger the magnitude of the shift

items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > Curve Shaper
items.name: Max Frequency - High Temperature
items.help:
Curve Shaper is an advanced overclocking tuning suite utilizing the same "Curve optimizer" steps. It changes variable voltage across all cores for finite (overlapping) frequency and temperature regions. This can be used to more precisely tune the voltage required by your system. 
In general, Low temperature corresponds to idle temps, Med Temperature corresponds to 1T/Gaming Workloads, and high temperature is for stress tests.
Additionally, Min and Low frequencies are idle/background tasks, Medium is high core count workloads, and high and Max frequency are for gaming and 1T workloads
These settings work as "bands" so you may find that for particular cases several settings impact the behavior. Ex, A workload running at 65 Celsius will likely be influenced by Low temp and Med temp values. Workloads lower than 65C will be more impacted by Low. Workloads above 65C will be more impacted by Medium.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > Curve Shaper > Max Frequency - High Temperature Sign
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > Curve Shaper
items.name: Max Frequency - High Temperature Sign
items.help: Determines the direction of the shift. Positive shifts the curve up to use higher voltages. Negative shifts the curve down to use lower voltages

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > Curve Shaper > Max Frequency - High Temperature Magnitude

items.name: Max Frequency - High Temperature Magnitude
items.help: Determines the magnitude of the shift to be made (entered in whole numbers) the larger the value entered the larger the magnitude of the shift

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > SoC Voltage > SoC Voltage

Stepping is 5mv. Voltage ranges allowed to be set will be limited outside of LN2 mode. If in LN2 mode (and CPU temp is below -40c) the allowable range of settable voltages will be extended.

items.name: CPU Frequency
items.help: Specifies a custom CPU core frequency. Should be combined with a custom CPU voltage. Power saving features for idle cores (e.g. cc6 sleep) remain active. Manual CPU OC overrides PBO settings.

rules.suppress_if: [Q0xaa]=0x1 NOT [Q0xa5]=0x1 NOT [Q0xa5]=0x4 NOT AND [Q0xa5]=0x9 NOT AND [Q0xa5]=0xa NOT AND OR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking > CPU Voltage
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking
items.name: CPU Voltage
items.help: Specifies a custom CPU core voltage (mV). Should be combined with a custom CPU core frequency. Power saving features for idle cores (e.g. cc6 sleep) remain active. stepping is 5mv. Voltage ranges allowed to be set will be limited outside of LN2 mode. If in LN2 mode (and CPU temp is below -40c) the allowable range of settable voltages will be extended.

rules.suppress_if: [Q0xaa]=0x1 NOT [Q0xa5]=0x1 NOT [Q0xa5]=0x4 NOT AND [Q0xa5]=0x9 NOT AND [Q0xa5]=0xa NOT AND OR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking > CPU Core Count Control > SMT Control
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual CPU Overclocking > CPU Core Count Control
items.name: SMT Control
items.help: Can be used to disable symmetric multithreading. To re-enable SMT, a POWER CYCLE is needed after selecting the 'Auto' option.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Manual iGPU Overclocking > GFX Voltage

items.name: GFX Voltage
items.help: Specifies a custom GFX core voltage (mV). Must be combined with a custom GFX frequency. GFX voltage is derived from SOC / uncore voltage rail. Power saving features (like GFX Pstates) remain active.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options > Nitro Rx Burst Length
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options
items.name: Nitro Rx Burst Length
items.help:
DQ Training Pattern Length -
  Higher number results in more robust training and longer runtime.
  Lower number results in less robust training and shorter runtime, but potentially less stability.

items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > DDR and Infinity Fabric Frequency/Timings > DDR Options > DDR Timing Configuration
items.name: Memory Target Speed
items.help:
Specifies the memory target speed in MT/s. The valid input is 2000 MT/s, 2400MT/s, and range of 3200MT/s ~ 12000 MT/s(stepping of 200 MT/s). The Value is in decimal.
The user input value will be rounded down to align with the stepping of 200MT/s.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > Precision Boost Overdrive
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive
items.name: Precision Boost Overdrive
items.help:
Precision Boost Overdrive:
  Enabled: Allows Processor to run beyond defined values for PPT, VDD_CPU EDC, VDD_CPU TDC, VDD_SOC EDC, VDD_SOC TDC to the limits of the board, and allows it to boost at higher voltages for longer durations than default operation.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > PBO Limits
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive
items.name: PBO Limits
items.help: Default: Loads AMD default socket power (PPT), electrically-limited VRM current (EDC), and thermally-limited VRM current (TDC) limits. Motherboard: Allows the processor to run according to increased PPT, EDC, and TDC limits defined by your motherboard. Manual: Allows the processor to ignore AMD default limits for PPT, EDC, and TDC and instead use manual values (up to the maximum capabilities of the of the motherboard).

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > PPT Limit [mW]
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive
items.name: PPT Limit [mW]
items.help: Adjust total CPU socket power delivery capability. Adjustable up to the limit supported by your motherboard.

rules.suppress_if: [Precision Boost Overdrive]=0x2 NOT [PBO Limits]=0x2 NOT OR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > TDC Limit [mA]
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive
items.name: TDC Limit [mA]
items.help: Adjust peak current from your motherboard's CPU core VRM phases in thermally-limited scenarios. Adjustable up to the limit supported by your motherboard.

rules.suppress_if: [Precision Boost Overdrive]=0x2 NOT [PBO Limits]=0x2 NOT OR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > EDC Limit [mA]
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive
items.name: EDC Limit [mA]
items.help: Adjust peak current from your motherboard CPU core VRM phases in electrically-limited scenarios. Adjustable up to the limit supported by your motherboard.

rules.suppress_if: [Precision Boost Overdrive]=0x2 NOT [PBO Limits]=0x2 NOT [Q0xa5]=0x1 NOT AND [Q0xa5]=0x4 NOT AND [Q0xa5]=0x9 NOT AND [Q0xa5]=0xa NOT AND OR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > GFX Curve Optimizer > GFX Curve Optimizer
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Precision Boost Overdrive > GFX Curve Optimizer
items.name: GFX Curve Optimizer
items.help: Allows the user to shift the GFX Voltage / Frequency (AVFS) curve to include higher voltages (positive values) or lower voltages (negative values). The larger the value entered the larger the magnitude of the voltage shift.

Value entered, combined with the sign above, is the used to send the SMU an GFX Curve Optimizer

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > VDDP Voltage Control > VDDP Voltage Control
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > VDDP Voltage Control
items.name: VDDP Voltage Control
items.help: Allows the user to adjust the VDDP voltage.'Manual' means set voltage for the DDR bus signaling (PHY),. 'Auto' means VDDP is system default.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > VDDP Voltage Control > VDDP Voltage Adjust
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > VDDP Voltage Control
items.name: VDDP Voltage Adjust
items.help: VDDP is a voltage for the DDR bus signaling (PHY), and it is derived from your DRAM Voltage (VDDIO_Mem). As a result, VDDP voltage in mV can approach but not exceed your DRAM Voltage. Stepping is 5mv

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > SoC/Uncore OC Mode > SoC/Uncore OC Mode
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > SoC/Uncore OC Mode
items.name: SoC/Uncore OC Mode
items.help: Forces CPU SoC/uncore components (e.g. Infinity Fabric, memory, and integrated graphics) to run at their maximum specified frequency at all times. May improve performance at the expense of idle power savings. On some products the ACPI sleep state (S3) may be disabled.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > SoC Voltage > SoC Voltage
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > SoC Voltage
items.name: SoC Voltage
items.help: Specifies the SoC/uncore voltage (VDD_SOC) in mV to support memory and Infinity Fabric overclocking. VDD_SOC also determines the GPU voltage on processors with integrated graphics. Voltage ranges allowed to be set will be limited outside of LN2 mode. If in LN2 mode (and CPU temp is below -40c) the allowable range of settable voltages will be extended.

rules.gray_out_if: [SoC/Uncore OC Mode]=0x1 NOT [Active Memory Timing Settings]=0x1 NOT AND [UCLK DIV1 MODE]=0xff AND [Infinity Fabric Frequency and Dividers]=0xffff AND

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > LN2 Mode > LN2 Mode
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > LN2 Mode
items.name: LN2 Mode
items.help: Enables settings that provide additional stability at extreme cold operating temperatures

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > VDD Misc > VDD Misc Control
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > VDD Misc
items.name: VDD Misc Control
items.help: Allows the user to adjust the VDD Misc voltage.'Manual' means set voltage for the GMI PHY,. 'Auto' means VDD MISC is system default.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > VDD Misc > VDD Misc Voltage
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > VDD Misc
items.name: VDD Misc Voltage
items.help: specific the VDD Misc Voltage in mV, definitely follow SVI3 type 2 Slave VID(500~5600mV step 10mV). Voltage ranges allowed to be set will be limited outside of LN2 mode. If in LN2 mode (and CPU temp is below -40c) the allowable range of settable voltages will be extended.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > LCLK Frequency Control > LCLK Frequency Control
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > LCLK Frequency Control
items.name: LCLK Frequency Control
items.help: AUTO: Default Settings. Manual: manually configure LCLK Frequency. Only specific frequencies are permitted; processor firmware will automatically round UP to the nearest permitted frequency.

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > LCLK Frequency Control > Minimun Frequency
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > LCLK Frequency Control
items.name: Minimun Frequency
items.help: Minimum LCLK Frequency. Set minimum and maximun to the same value for fixed frequency operation.Range:150MHz ~ 2500MHz

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > LCLK Frequency Control > Maximum Frequency
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > LCLK Frequency Control
items.name: Maximum Frequency
items.help: Maximum LCLK Frequency. Set minimum and maximun to the same value for fixed frequency operation.Range:150MHz ~ 2500MHz

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control > VDDIO Ctrl
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control
items.name: VDDIO Ctrl
items.help: Allows the user to adjust the VDDIO voltage.'Manual' means set DIMM VDD/VDDQ will synchronize to APU VDDIO. 'Separate' means independent control of APU VDDIO,DIMM VDD/VDDQ.Note, that running VDDQ != VDD is non-standard and may casue memory stability issues. Take care that during ramp down and ramp up,the VDDq-VDD voltage must less than 200mv.

items.name: PMIC VDD Stepping Control
items.help: PMIC VDD Stepping Control by R2B, select 10mv will set PMIC R2B BIT5

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control > DIMM VDD Adjust
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control
items.name: DIMM VDD Adjust
items.help: Adjust DIMM Power Supply, stepping is 10mV. Range is from 800mV to 1430mV.Take care that during ramp down and ramp up,the VDDq-VDD voltage must less than 200mv.

rules.suppress_if: [Q0xa6]=0x2 [PMIC VDD Stepping Control]=0x1 OR [VDDIO Ctrl]=0x1 NOT [VDDIO Ctrl]=0x2 NOT AND OR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control > DIMM VDD Adjust
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control
items.name: DIMM VDD Adjust
items.help: Adjust DIMM Power Supply, stepping is 10mV. Range is from 800mV to 1650mV.Take care that during ramp down and ramp up,the VDDq-VDD voltage must less than 200mv.

rules.suppress_if: [Q0xa6]=0x2 NOT [PMIC VDD Stepping Control]=0x1 NOT AND [VDDIO Ctrl]=0x1 NOT [VDDIO Ctrl]=0x2 NOT AND OR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control > DIMM VDDQ Adjust
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control
items.name: DIMM VDDQ Adjust
items.help: Adjust DIMM DQ Power Supply, stepping is 10mV. Range is from 800mV to 1430mV.Take care that during ramp down and ramp up, the VDDq-VDD voltage must less than 200mv.And Vpp must always equal or greater than VDDQ

rules.suppress_if: [Q0xa6]=0x2 [PMIC VDDQ Stepping Control]=0x1 OR [VDDIO Ctrl]=0x2 NOT OR

items.help: Adjust DIMM DQ Power Supply, stepping is 10mV. Range is from 800mV to 1650mV.Take care that during ramp down and ramp up, the VDDq-VDD voltage must less than 200mv.And Vpp must always equal or greater than VDDQ

rules.suppress_if: [Q0xa6]=0x2 NOT [PMIC VDDQ Stepping Control]=0x1 NOT AND [VDDIO Ctrl]=0x2 NOT OR

items.path: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control > Enable Platform PMIC Control
items.menu: AMD Overclocking Option > Accept > Onboard Voltage Control > VDDIO Voltage Control
items.name: Enable Platform PMIC Control
items.help: When Enable Platform PMIC Control is enabled, the DDR PMIC voltages are not adjusted by processor FW, and may be adjusted directly by EC or other platform based mechanism.

rules.suppress_if: [VDDIO Ctrl]=0x2 NOT ; [Q0xa5]=0x1 NOT [Q0xa5]=0x4 NOT AND [Q0xa5]=0x9 NOT AND [Q0xa5]=0xa NOT AND
